summary: Queue writer-bound callbacks asynchronously before they enter the blocking pool

replay.detail: No claim, projection or replay changes.

schema.detail: Worker admission is in memory; the schema and its digest are unchanged.

rules.detail: Writer foreground ordering, fences, background loans and durable acknowledgements retain their existing queue semantics.

compatibility.detail: Each WriterConnection admits at most 32 top-level writer-bound callbacks before spawn_blocking. Mutation handlers, local replication receive, mailbox control and daemon maintenance use this admission. Dependent same-writer callbacks share their parent's capacity. Reads and health retain independent capacity. Raw synchronous writer calls and non-store blocking work remain ungated; Tokio's global blocking-thread limit is unchanged because provider and nested-callback dependencies need a separate design.

downtime.detail: No data migration; admission settings take effect on process restart.

manual.detail: SMALLCLAIMS_MAX_WRITE_WORKERS sets the positive per-writer worker count. Missing, invalid, zero or oversized values use 32, matching read-worker configuration. This bounds the writer-stall thread amplifier, not writer-hold duration or reader-cache memory.

recovery.detail: Binary swap-back needs no migration. Pending helper admission can be dropped without starting work; started or detached callbacks retain capacity until completion, including on panic. API mutation completion behavior is unchanged.
